editorial.headline: Public Stewardship of Indonesia’s Historic Sites and Monuments
editorial.standfirst: This government-led activity safeguards historic places, monuments and visitor-accessible archaeological sites of cultural, scientific and religious significance.
editorial.body:
This activity is the public stewardship of historic places and monuments: the operation and preservation of heritage created through human intervention in the environment, whether landscapes, parks, buildings or sites. Its remit embraces built cultural heritage and natural heritage whose importance lies in history, science and culture, as well as places valued for education and religion. Temples, saints’ tombs and historic mosques illustrate the kind of places contemplated by the record, but the underlying purpose is broader: keeping significant heritage places operational, protected and meaningful to the public.

The work is explicitly governmental. It includes operating and conserving historic sites and buildings, alongside archaeological sites open to visitors. That framing matters. This is not merely the maintenance of an old structure or the presentation of an attraction; it is public responsibility for places whose significance is judged across historical, scientific, educational, religious and cultural dimensions. The slim record lists no business-scale categories open to registration, reinforcing the activity’s institutional character.

Nationally, the position for foreign investment is closed. The foreign-ownership ceiling is zero, so a foreign investor cannot hold a stake in an entity registered for this activity under the national PMA position recorded here. The cited basis is Presidential Regulation 10/2021 and 49/2021. For a founder assessing the code, that is the decisive national answer: the activity is reserved from PMA participation, not simply subject to a reduced foreign share.

Bali reaches the same practical conclusion for PMA registration: the activity is marked closed and blocked today. The Bali record also makes an important distinction about why. Its medium-high or high-risk treatment means it is not blocked by Bali’s island-wide moratorium, which applies to low and medium-low risk KBLI activities; the applicable classification should nevertheless be verified for the specific address. In other words, the Bali outcome is closed, but it should not be casually attributed to the moratorium. The clean conclusion is that foreign investors cannot register this activity in Bali today, while government stewardship remains at the centre of what the code describes.
